item.description:
### Added
- **Add to Music** in the Disc menu adds an earlier rip's album to Apple's Music app at any time, and when "Add each disc to Music" is on in Settings, the toolbar has the button too. If Music seems to have the album already, Silverside asks first. - An earlier rip of a disc of a set shows the disc's own title in a box set of multiple albums or titles, and so does a disc in a drive. - Use Each Disc's Sleeve now also works for a box set whose images in the Cover Art Archive don't name a disc, when there is one front for each disc in the discs' order. The picker marks each front with its disc, so you can check them first. - The report of a copy-protected disc, such as one with Cactus Data Shield, explains the C2 errors that come about every 6 seconds in every track: the drive fills in audio that the protection took out, so they are not damage. - Search MusicBrainz… takes a link to a release in MusicBrainz, or its ID, for a disc that the lookup did not find: paste it in the search field. A link to a release group lists its releases. The "Not in MusicBrainz" chip opens the search too. - The chip that adds a disc ID to a release found by its track lengths, its barcode, or a search opens MusicBrainz at that release, with its discs to choose from, not at a search for it. - More Results, under Search MusicBrainz…'s results, shows the next 25 releases that MusicBrainz found, up to 100. - Help › Support Silverside, and Leave a Tip in the About window, open the page where you can leave a tip. Silverside stays free. - The About window names Silvercode Studio, which makes Silverside, with a link to its website.
### Changed
- FLAC albums can now go into Music too. Music cannot play FLAC, so it gets Apple Lossless or AAC copies, made in their own folder (Settings › General › Apple Music), never in the library and never over a file. When Music copies files into its own folder, as it does at first, Silverside deletes its copies. - An album that Music has already is not added again after a rip or Encode. - The Rip button has a new icon: a drive's pickup over the disc. During a rip, the level bars hang below the pickup and its laser's spot pulses on the disc.
### Fixed
- Search MusicBrainz… looked for your words in album titles only, so an artist's name did not help, and a release with a common title, such as *Valhalla*, could be missing from the results. Now it looks for them in the artists too, as MusicBrainz's own search does, and a catalog number, such as CK 67862, finds its release. So does `silverside album --search`. - A rip just after you added the disc ID in MusicBrainz could still say "nearly the same TOC", until Look Up Metadata: the release's details came from Silverside's cache, from before the disc ID. A release whose details lack a disc ID that MusicBrainz now lists is looked up again. - On an earlier rip of a set's disc, the Cover Art Archive picker said that the image you choose goes on every disc. It now says that Silverside asks next whether the image is for that disc only or for every disc, as it always did. - A name edit, Update the Library, a new cover, Change Release, or a set's album gain wrote every tag of a FLAC, Apple Lossless, or AAC file again, so tags that another program had added were lost, such as a genre typed in a tag editor. Those tags now stay. MP3, AIFF, and WAV files keep only Silverside's tags. - `silverside tags --json` printed a note before the JSON for a folder of album folders ("add --recursive"), and `silverside cdtext --json` printed one in place of it for a disc without CD-Text, so programs could not read the output. The notes now go to standard error.

### Added
- The `silverside` command line tool has two new commands for albums that Silverside did not rip: `tags` shows an album folder's tags and covers, and `album` gives it the tags and cover art of its MusicBrainz release. For more, see Help › Command Line Tool, or [docs/cli.md](https://github.com/SilvercodeStudio/Silverside/blob/main/docs/cli.md).
### Changed
- A DTS-CD's album that keeps the stream is now named for it, such as "Forever Yours (DTS 5.1)", and the decoded copy beside it "Forever Yours (5.1)": the stream plays as static without a DTS decoder, so it is the one that needs the label. The decoded album alone keeps the album's own title. Albums encoded before keep their names. - The welcome window and Help now advise System Settings › CDs & DVDs › Ignore, so that Music does not open when a disc goes in. Music's Show CD setting is still there for people who want Music to open. - Building from source: `make install-cli-local` installs the command in `~/.local`, and `make install` is gone. `make` now stops when it runs as root: `sudo make install` left build files that only root could replace, and the next build failed. The app's Install Command Line Tool… puts the command in `/usr/local`.
### Fixed
- A rip slowed to a crawl, or stopped, while the display slept, until the Mac was woken. While a rip, an encoding, or a repair runs, the Mac now stays awake and the display can sleep. The command line tool does the same. - A drive that AccurateRip's list of drives does not have, such as Apple's USB SuperDrive, no longer stops the rip and asks for its read offset. The rip finds the offset from the disc's tracks in AccurateRip, and rips of later discs confirm it. Settings › Drives says when rips confirm an offset other than one set by hand. - A rip that fails before it reads, such as for a drive whose offset is not known, now shows the whole message above the tracks, with a button to the drive's settings where it helps. Before, the status bar cut it to one line. - Saving a release's artwork no longer fails on an image that the Cover Art Archive keeps as a PDF or GIF, such as a booklet: it is saved as it is.

First public release.
### Added
- The `silverside` command-line tool comes inside the app. Silverside › Install Command Line Tool… (or Settings › General) links it into `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`, with its zsh, bash, and fish completions, so each update of the app updates the command too.
### Changed
- Silverside downloads as a disk image: open it, and drag Silverside to the Applications folder.
### Fixed
- On a copy-protected disc with a short audio track after its data track, the last track before the data took in the gap between the disc's sessions: minutes of noise and unreadable sectors, so it was never verified. It now ends with its music, and the release in MusicBrainz can fit the disc. - A library on a NAS that was not yet connected when Silverside opened made its rips look moved or deleted, and they stayed so. Such rips now show as offline and keep their place in Recent Rips, and Silverside looks again when a disk or network share is connected or disconnected. - Rip History could show one rip twice, and leave out another, when a disc was ripped again into the same folder; opening the earlier rip showed the later one. Each rip now has a row of its own and opens as itself, marked "Replaced" when a later rip of the disc took its place. - The video of a CD+G disc's graphics stayed in the rip's folder when the rip was not verified and was accepted and encoded later. It now moves into the album folder with the music, as a verified rip's video does. - A CD+EG disc that sends its display settings split over two symbols, as *Divacore* does, showed only its first picture in 256 colors: the pictures after it never drew. Its video now shows every picture.
